tldr: Headlines across 7 outlet clusters assert that Nigerian security forces conducted the country's largest single-day rescue, freeing over 300 kidnapping victims in a joint military-police operation; domestic Nigerian outlets and AP add a political credit-claiming layer centred on President Tinubu.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame the rescue through an explicitly partisan lens — 'Kano APC chieftain hails Tinubu' — converting a national security story into ruling-party credit-claiming; also uniquely reports 176 abductees rather than the full 308 figure cited by every other outlet.
Only headline to foreground the duration of the effort ('six-month operation in Kwara, Niger forests'), reframing the story from a sudden breakthrough to the conclusion of a protracted campaign.

bottom_line: The headline layer delivers a near-uniform security-success narrative — Nigerian forces freed 300+ abductees in a record single-day operation — while Nigerian domestic press and AP overlay political credit for President Tinubu and his ruling party.
